name: The library index
note: One entry per thing in the library: the seven exemplars of Exemplar Pack v2 and the two assistants. Every entry carries a use_it_when line, the scenario it answers, its inputs, its output, its limits and a tested_on line that says only what has been observed; the exemplar entries are taken from each sheet's own exemplar page (section 5) and results table, checked 25 Oct 2026. Synthetic data only. Edit this file; INDEX.md is rendered from it with: node library/search.js --md

entries.name: Conversation Brief Assistant
entries.use_it_when: After a client conversation, when a partner needs a one-page brief to read in three minutes before the next meeting, and you have the transcript with numbered turns.
entries.scenario: One client conversation transcript to a one-page partner brief
entries.inputs: The filled input template as one message: engagement question, stakeholder role, date, who it is for, permitted organisation names, any leave-out notes, then the transcript
entries.output: A one-page brief: headline, findings tagged FACT, VIEW, RISK, GAP or ASK with turn references, quotes word for word, open questions, next step
entries.limits: Declines, one line each at the top, then delivers the rest: inventing or sharpening a quote; attributing a statement the transcript does not show; keeping a personal name (keeps the role label). Leaves out personal matters about an identifiable person. Asks for any missing required input. One transcript per run.
entries.tested_on: Claude Project, Sonnet 5.5 at Low: 4 of 5 cases matched, rehearsal passed, both declines held. Custom GPT, GPT-5.6 Sol at High: 2 of 5, not passed. Final runs 7 Oct 2026, five synthetic transcripts, one run per case. The Claude miss: T2, a figure given inside a concern tagged FACT where the check expects RISK; v1.5 carries the rule and has not been run.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block
entries.where: The exemplar pack and the tested v1.4 set, both kept on the owner's machine

entries.name: Column Mapper
entries.use_it_when: Many Excel or CSV files carry the same information under different headers and you need one table: monthly returns from many sites, survey exports from several waves, trackers kept by different teams.
entries.scenario: 500 Excel files, same information, inconsistent column names, consolidate automatically
entries.inputs: The header listing (every header with a count and a sample value) and your canonical field list: name, meaning, type; seven to fifteen fields is normal
entries.output: The mapping table with every doubtful header flagged for your decision, then the Power Query that applies it, piloted on fifty files before the rest
entries.limits: Never sees your files and never fills a gap. Fewer than ten files: open them instead. Files with different information, not just different headers, are a data model question. Mixed date formats always need your decision. Headers in more than one language untested. Over 200 distinct headers goes in two halves.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block

entries.name: Process Mapper
entries.use_it_when: A team wants a process automated or improved and cannot write down what it does today: shortlisting, expense approval, document review, inbound request triage.
entries.scenario: 5,000 CVs to shortlist, and the team cannot explain its own process
entries.inputs: The filled template and the last three real cases, names and identifiers removed, answered one question at a time in the chat
entries.output: A one-page draft process map: steps, decision points, handoffs, the unresolved rules for the lead to decide; signed, it goes to the Runbook Writer
entries.limits: Records what was done, not what should be done. Needs at least three recent cases. Refuses to score or shortlist anything. Rare exceptions appear only if a case hit one. Not for cases that cannot be described without personal details.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block

entries.name: Fit Check
entries.use_it_when: Anyone brings a recurring task and asks for it to be automated, especially when the tool is already named in the ask; use it before the working session.
entries.scenario: A partner spends five hours a week on one task and wants it automated
entries.inputs: The task template, filled by the requester: what triggers it, inputs and where they come from, output and reader, where the hours go, the tools they have, whether any input holds confidential or personal data
entries.output: The task split into steps, each labelled RULES, LANGUAGE or JUDGEMENT with the check for every LANGUAGE step; one verdict (NOT AI, AUTOMATION FIRST, AI-ASSISTED or HYBRID); the minimum version to build this week; what is deferred and why
entries.limits: Works from the description, so a vague template gives a vague split. Never recommends a tool the requester does not have. Never promises the task can run unattended. A step with no confirmed data route is marked blocked and treated as JUDGEMENT. Not for one-off tasks.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block

entries.name: Pattern Log
entries.use_it_when: Weekly after office hours to log the asks; monthly to find what crossed the threshold; whenever a lead asks how many people want something; whenever the answer to a request is no and the requesters need to hear it properly.
entries.scenario: The same request arrives ten times a month, and what to say when the answer is no
entries.inputs: The week's office-hours notes, one line per ask; at month end, the rows; when product says no, their words
entries.output: Log rows in nine columns with a corrected 'what it really was'; the monthly grouping; a one-action memo in roles only for any group over the threshold; the reply to the requesters when the answer is no
entries.limits: A log, not a ticket queue. Never attaches a name. Its reading of 'what it really was' is a first guess, so the correction step is mandatory. The threshold is a number the owner set in the knowledge file. One action per memo.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block

entries.name: Runbook Writer
entries.use_it_when: A process is mapped and signed, the only tools are chat interfaces, and someone needs to run it next week without the analyst in the room.
entries.scenario: Only chat interfaces, no API, no connectors, no co-work tool: which steps get AI applied
entries.inputs: The signed process map, the tool list and the data rule, confirmed with the process owner in writing
entries.output: A runbook with every step labelled FETCH, CHAT, DECIDE or OUT OF REACH; every CHAT step has a paste block and a check; a role on every DECIDE
entries.limits: With chat only, the person is the API: every FETCH is their time. It makes the CHAT steps consistent and checkable; it does not shorten the process. Steps that select people are never CHAT. Unsigned maps are refused. Writes the runbook, does not run it.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.
entries.shape: Claude Project and custom GPT, one instruction block

entries.name: Right-Size
entries.use_it_when: Every time an exemplar passes its test log, before it goes in the library, to let evidence set the default tier; and whenever a consultant asks which model to use for a task.
entries.scenario: Consultants reach for the most powerful model at 1 a.m.; teach cost efficiency
entries.inputs: The results of Test 1, the edge case and the refusal case run on the tier below the one the exemplar was built on, saved outputs included
entries.output: The lowest tier that passed the three cases, the tested-on line for the exemplar page, and a three-sentence note for the consultant with no cost words
entries.limits: Hands untested prompts the check instead of a recommendation. Not for general 'which model is best' questions. Knows nothing about any platform's pricing or limits and says nothing about them.
entries.tested_on: Not yet run. Instruction block, five cases and the Test 1 answer key written 1 Oct 2026; the results table is empty.

entries.name: Meeting Tracker Assistant
entries.use_it_when: Meeting transcripts land in a folder every week and someone needs a running list of who committed to what, by when, with the questions the model would otherwise guess.
entries.scenario: A folder of meeting transcripts to an action tracker with owners and due dates, kept week to week
entries.inputs: A folder of transcripts (header with meeting, date and attendees; numbered lines) and a contacts table that stands in for a CRM
entries.output: The tracker appended with this week's actions, each with its source line, owner, company, role and due date; a run log; a summary and a one-page action board
entries.limits: Synthetic transcripts and a synthetic contacts table; one folder; no scheduling; no email; no external system connected; append and status change only, never a rewrite; stops at four gates
entries.tested_on: Harness run, 25 Oct 2026: claude-opus-5-5 (high) 5 of 5, decline held; claude-haiku-5-5 4 of 5, decline held. Three runs by hand before that: 4 of 5, then 5 of 5. Every run recorded in eval/results.
entries.shape: Claude Project skill plus a Node.js tool server with ten tools; the model calls the tools itself

entries.name: Prompt Drill Coach
entries.use_it_when: Someone wants to practise writing a brief from a fuzzy request and be graded on it, with the model sheet shown only after they have written their own.
entries.scenario: Office hours without a coach in the room: a fuzzy request, a timed attempt, a grade and one fix
entries.inputs: A fuzzy request from a consulting setting (served by the coach) and the person's own written sheet
entries.output: A score against the six components, the line most likely to be misread, the one fix, a model sheet, and a session log entry
entries.limits: Grades the person's sheet; never writes the sheet for them; a coach for the owner's own practice; would go through five cases before anyone else used it
entries.tested_on: A session log of the owner's own reps since 5 Oct 2026. No five-case rehearsal; the block's own rule is that it would go through the five cases before anyone else used it.
entries.status: in use by the owner only
entries.shape: Custom GPT (and the prompt-drill skill in Claude)
entries.where: The custom GPT 'Prompt Drill Coach' in the owner's ChatGPT account, saved to himself; the same block runs as the prompt-drill skill in Claude
